history.summary: A major Shakti Peetha at Chandrapur (Chandkhuri), on a hill at the confluence of the Mand and Mahanadi rivers - legend says the left cheek of Goddess Sati fell here, and the goddess appeared in King Chandrahas's dream ordering him to build the temple; a companion shrine to her younger sister Nathaldai stands on an island in the Mahanadi that, devotees say, never submerges even in flood. The shrine has a black-stone murti of the goddess (named for her moon-like radiance, 'Chandrahasini'), a saffron entrance arch and a mirror hall, with tableau shrines depicting the Samudra Manthan, Krishna Leela, Mahishasura vadha and the Char Dham. Construction claims CONFLICT across sources: Kalachuri ~1050 CE (heritage portals), 12th-century Kalchuri with 19th-century reconstruction (templeyatri), ~1500 years old (velpu), and 16th-century Gond king Dhundhya Ram Shah (a YouTube account of the legend). CSV TOWN CORRECTION: 'Rajnandgaon' is WRONG - the temple is at Chandrapur/Chandkhuri, Sakti district (formerly Janjgir-Champa). Coordinates are the Chandrapur village geocode (approximate; the temple stands on a hill by the river confluence).

name: Chandrahasini Devi Temple, Chandkhuri
town_description: Chandrapur (also called Chandkhuri) is a small town on the banks of the Mahanadi at the confluence of the Mand river, now in Sakti district of Chhattisgarh. It is best known as a major Shakti pilgrimage centre, home to the Chandrahasini Temple on its riverside hill and the Nathaldai island shrine. Devotees come from across Chhattisgarh and neighbouring Odisha, especially during Navratri.
